office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 47th District (Kent, Auburn, Covington and Maple Valley area of South King County), serving a two-year term writing state law and budgets.
race_blurb: A rematch of 2024: Democratic incumbent and House Speaker Pro Tempore Chris Stearns faces Republican Ted Cooke, a software tester and longtime party officer. They differ on taxes, parental rights, gender policy, climate and density.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative and House Speaker Pro Tempore; a Navajo attorney, former Auburn City Councilmember and former Washington State Gambling Commission chair.
highlights: Calls reproductive and gender-affirming care 'a human right' the Legislature must protect [S3]
Voted yes on ESSB 6346, the 2026 millionaires' tax that I-645 would repeal [S5]
Voted yes on ESHB 1296 (2025), the parental-rights amendments I-1 would undo [S6]
Sponsored a clean energy infrastructure bill (HB 1461) signed into law [S2]
Endorsed by Gov. Ferguson, Rep. Adam Smith, the mayors of Auburn, Kent and Covington, and Washington Conservation Action [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million; no separate campaign statement on taxes.

spending.basis: Runs on delivered investment in affordable housing and behavioral health, and pledges to 'fight for investments in families' including universal childcare.

housing.basis: Cites expanding affordable housing as a result and priority; served on the King County Affordable Housing Commission.

climate.basis: Sponsored clean energy infrastructure legislation and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated carbon-pricing position.

social.basis: Repeatedly calls reproductive and gender-affirming care a human right, calls Dobbs 'unconscionable', and cites recognition by Pro-Choice Washington.

parental-rights.basis: Single record item: voted yes on ESHB 1296, which amended the I-2081 parental-rights law; no campaign statement on the topic.

tech.basis: Sponsored HB 1221 on data privacy and security, which passed the Senate.

experience.basis: Sitting House Speaker Pro Tempore and committee vice chair with bills signed into law; former city councilmember.

candidates.summary: Republican software tester and team lead from Covington, a precinct committee officer since 2009 and former King County GOP 2nd Vice Chair. He lost this seat to Stearns in 2024.
highlights: Would freeze new taxes, eliminate taxes on income, property and fuel, and audit every state office [S1]
Would 'restore full parental rights in education' and post school curricula online for parental review [S1][S4]
Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender' [S1]
Would end cap-and-trade and lower or eliminate the gas tax [S4]
Prefers 'starter homes with yards over high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia' [S1]

taxes.basis: Would freeze all new taxes and eliminate income, property and fuel taxes, and wants the capital gains tax eliminated.

spending.basis: Would audit every state office and program, cut waste, and stop increases in government spending.

housing.basis: Would ease the Growth Management Act, streamline permitting and cut taxes to spur building, while opposing state-driven high-density apartments.

safety.basis: Public safety first; would let police act on reasonable suspicion rather than probable cause and keep 'anti-police' members off use-of-force review boards.

climate.basis: Would end cap-and-trade (the Climate Commitment Act's mechanism) and eliminate fuel taxes to cut energy costs.

local-control.basis: Opposes 'high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia', would ease the Growth Management Act, and would end legislative commissions.

social.basis: Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender'; a single repeated pamphlet line, with no other gender or reproductive policy detail.

parental-rights.basis: Would 'restore full parental rights in education', give parents 'oversight of children and education', and post all curricula online for parental review.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; party officer and 2024 challenger.
